cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Case series and surveys suggest most patients on SSRIs tolerate cannabis without major interaction, though anxiety, jitteriness, or tachycardia can be amplified — especially with high-THC products. No consistent change in sertraline serum levels has been demonstrated.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: If combining, start with a low-THC or CBD-dominant product and watch for increased anxiety, racing heart, or new jitteriness. Tell your prescriber about any new mood symptoms.

sources.label: Cannabis and Mental Health: It's Complicated (NIDA Research Report)
Cannabis pharmacokinetics and interactions (British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 2018)

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Both fluoxetine and THC are metabolized by CYP enzymes (fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6 and CYP2C19). A clinically significant interaction is rarely reported, but additive effects on mood and rare reports of increased anxiety or tachycardia are documented.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: Observe for new or worsening anxiety, restlessness, or palpitations, particularly with high-THC products. Discuss any change in mood with your prescriber before adjusting your dose.

sources.label: Cannabis pharmacokinetics and interactions (British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 2018)
Medical cannabis and neuropsychiatric drug interactions (Journal of Clinical Pharmacy and Therapeutics, 2022)

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Surveys and case reports indicate most patients on escitalopram tolerate cannabis, with infrequent reports of amplified anxiety, jitteriness, or tachycardia — more often with high-THC products. No consistent effect on escitalopram serum levels is documented.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: Start low with THC and watch for increased anxiety, restlessness, or racing heart. Tell your prescriber about any new mood symptoms before changing your dose.

sources.label: Cannabis pharmacokinetics and interactions (British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 2018)
Medical cannabis and neuropsychiatric drug interactions (Journal of Clinical Pharmacy and Therapeutics, 2022)

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Citalopram is largely CYP2C19 metabolized; THC and CBD share these pathways. Reported interactions are uncommon and typically mild (anxiety, jitteriness), but QT-interval caution with citalopram means patients with cardiac risk factors warrant care.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: If you have a known cardiac condition or take other QT-prolonging drugs, be especially careful and talk to your prescriber before combining with cannabis.

sources.label: Cannabis pharmacokinetics and interactions (British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 2018)
Medical cannabis and neuropsychiatric drug interactions (Journal of Clinical Pharmacy and Therapeutics, 2022)

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Both alprazolam and cannabis (especially THC) produce central-nervous-system depression. Reports describe amplified sedation, dizziness, reduced motor coordination, and rare excess impairment. The risk scales with THC dose and is not a predictable serum-level change.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: Expect additive sedation and impaired coordination — do not drive. Start with a low-THC product, avoid sudden dose increases, and tell your prescriber before changing either medication.

sources.label: The pharmacological and physiological interactions between cannabis and benzodiazepines (CNS Drugs, 2019)
Drug interactions with cannabis and cannabinoids (Brown University Therapeutic Advances in Drug Safety, 2022)

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Lorazepam and cannabis share sedative effects on the central nervous system. Reports describe additive drowsiness, ataxia, and impaired reaction time. The risk rises with THC dose; CBD-dominant products appear less problematic in surveys but are not risk-free.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: Do not drive or operate machinery. Start with a low-THC product and keep the dose stable. Tell your prescriber if you feel overly sedated.

sources.label: The pharmacological and physiological interactions between cannabis and benzodiazepines (CNS Drugs, 2019)

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Clonazepam and THC both depress the central nervous system. Additive sedation, dizziness, and impaired motor coordination are reported; seizure-threshold effects in patients taking clonazepam for epilepsy warrant individualized review.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: Avoid driving and keep the THC dose low and stable. If clonazepam is for seizures, do not stop or change it without your prescriber.

sources.label: The pharmacological and physiological interactions between cannabis and benzodiazepines (CNS Drugs, 2019)
Drug interactions with cannabis and cannabinoids (Therapeutic Advances in Drug Safety, 2022)

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Oxycodone and cannabis both depress respiration and alertness; observational studies of chronic-pain patients often show opioid-sparing effects but also amplified sedation and rare reports of excess somnolence. CYP3A4 interactions are possible but not reliably clinically significant.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: Start low with THC, avoid sudden opioid dose changes, and watch for unusual drowsiness or slow breathing. Tell your prescriber before combining; some patients use cannabis to reduce opioid dose, but never adjust on your own.

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Hydrocodone and cannabis share sedative and respiratory-depressant effects. Reports describe additive drowsiness and dizziness; CYP3A4-mediated clearance changes are possible but inconsistent. Patients with hepatic impairment warrant closer monitoring.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: Keep THC low and avoid driving. Watch for excess sedation and tell your prescriber before combining.

sources.label: Cannabis and opioids: pharmacologic parallels and interactions (Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 2021)

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Morphine and THC both depress the central nervous system. Studies of cancer and chronic-pain patients report opioid-sparing effects but also amplified sedation and rare excess somnolence; respiratory depression risk scales with opioid dose.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: Start with a low-THC product, avoid driving, and watch for slow or shallow breathing. Never change your morphine dose without your prescriber.

sources.label: Cannabis and opioids: pharmacologic parallels and interactions (Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 2021)

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Case reports describe international normalized ratio (INR) increases and bleeding events when cannabis is started or dose-escalated in patients on warfarin, consistent with CYP2C9 inhibition by cannabinoids. The interaction is clinically meaningful and requires INR monitoring.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: If you start, stop, or change cannabis, tell the clinician managing your warfarin and have your INR checked. Watch for unusual bruising or bleeding.

sources.label: Cannabis pharmacokinetics and interactions (British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 2018)

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Apixaban is a P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 substrate; cannabinoids can modulate these pathways. Clinical reports are limited, but the theoretical risk of altered anticoagulant exposure warrants caution, especially in older adults or patients on strong inhibitors.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: Tell the clinician managing your apixaban before starting cannabis, and report any unusual bleeding or bruising. Routine INR is not used with apixaban, so monitoring is clinical.

sources.label: Cannabis pharmacokinetics and interactions (British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 2018)
Medical cannabis and drug interactions: a review of clinical and preclinical evidence (Advances in Therapy, 2022)

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Both diphenhydramine and cannabis produce sedation; additive drowsiness, dry mouth, and impaired coordination are reported. The interaction is usually mild and short-lived but worsens with THC dose and age.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: Expect more drowsiness and dry mouth. Avoid driving, and keep THC low. Tell your prescriber if you rely on diphenhydramine for sleep or allergies.

Drug interactions with cannabis and cannabinoids (Therapeutic Advances in Drug Safety, 2022)

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Stimulants and cannabis have opposing effects on alertness and heart rate; surveys describe variable combinations of amplified anxiety, palpitations, or perceived reduced stimulant effect. No consistent serum-level change is documented.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: Watch for racing heart, anxiety, or a rebound tiredness when the cannabis wears off. Keep THC low and steady, and tell your prescriber about any new mood or heart symptoms.

cannabisInteraction.mechanism: Modafinil and cannabis have opposing effects on alertness and sleep. CYP3A4 interactions are theoretically possible; reports of amplified anxiety or perceived reduced stimulant effect are infrequent and mild.
cannabisInteraction.commonGuidance: Watch for new anxiety, palpitations, or trouble sleeping, particularly with high-THC products. Keep the THC dose stable and tell your prescriber about any change in mood or sleep.
